questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Possibilities outside of uni; hiking, mountains, skiing, etc.
- A university with a great international environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. UBC's website is well managed and pretty straight forward for exchange and international students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: GoGlobal had an introduction event for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were many different locations that we could apply for but I think only half of the incoming students received housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in an small house/flat with a fully working kitchen. Not equipped though - we had to get out own kitchen stuff.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Kitchens are not equipped so that's an extra expense.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After receiving my exchange spot at UBC and my UBC student number I was sent all the relevant information via my KU e-mail. I had to browse through the courses offered on UBC's database. They had short descriptions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always e-mail the university but it was not necessary for me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the four classes that I wanted. I ended up registering for five and then I just dropped one of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry. You have some time to change your mind when you arrive at the host institution.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My experience was that the level was a little bit lower than UCPH, more experience based than theoretical - but I did choose introduction courses and more creative courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had a mix of big lectures with no student participation and smaller classes with a lot of class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTH 206: Witches, Vampires, and Zombies: Anthropology of the Supernatural
GRSJ 307 - Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Popular Culture
CRWR 205 - Introduction to writing creative nonfiction
CRWR 206 - Introduction to writing for the screen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was really happy with all of my courses but if you're interested in films I would recommend Introduction to writing for the screen. It was interesting to try to write my own stuff and get a more practical insight in to how a film/series comes about.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Kitchen gear.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and food in generel is quite expensive. That was definitely my biggest expense.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds! So many different clubs and associations you could join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A lot of my friends joined the VOC (Varsity Outdoors Club). They arranged a lot of outdoor activities and overnight trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains! Hike, ski, whatever. It's beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Canadian people are super nice and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Probably that most uni students are quite young.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved that when you get on the bus, you actually greet the bus driver and when you get off again, everyone thanks them!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The work load can be quite extensive.
Use the activities and associations available.
Enjoy your weekends and go on a lot of trips!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of courses take attendance.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being surround by a completely different nature and environment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The pressure of having to enjoy it all. Just relax, you can't do stuff all the time and you don't have to enjoy every single minute of it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
